findings.message: the pattern matches 10 of 20 sample lines. It must match every one: a line it misses is dropped entirely, not partly parsed. The first it misses is 'Oct 14 08:00:56 dhcp dhcpd[3163]: DHCPREQUEST for 10.10.5.14 from 02:48:95:17:1b:b5 (ws-ops-004) via eth0'. Of the 4 patterns, the closest to it is '^%{SYSLOGTIMESTAMP} %{HOSTNAME} dhcpd\\[%{POSINT}\\]: DHCP(?:ACK|NAK) on %{IP:dst_ip} to %{MAC:client_mac}(?: \\(%{NOTSPACE'. the pattern matches up to %{IP:dst_ip}, which fails on ']: DHCPREQUEST for 10.10.5.14 from 02:48' It also misses lines of other shapes: 'Oct 14 08:01:32 dhcp dhcpd[3163]: DHCPREQUEST for 10.10.1.12 from 02:5a:b6:14:8f:30 (ws-it-002) via eth0'; 'Oct 14 08:02:37 dhcp dhcpd[3163]: DHCPREQUEST for 10.20.7.13 from 02:3f:f8:b2:e4:6f (ws-general-003) via eth0'; 'Oct 14 08:04:06 dhcp dhcpd[3163]: DHCPREQUEST for 10.20.7.12 from 02:62:80:94:c7:13 (ws-general-002) via eth0'. If this line is a VARIANT of the others - an extra word, a field that is sometimes absent - make that part optional with (?:...)? rather than writing a second pattern. If it is a DIFFERENT KIND of message - different words, not one more of them - add a pattern for it to `alternatives`, reusing the same capture name for the same value.

the IR maps 'host', 'outcome', but no pattern captures them: the patterns capture only 'client_mac', 'dst_ip', 'hostname', 'iface', 'offer_number', 'server_port', 'src_ip'. A mapping whose key is never extracted leaves its ECS field empty on every line. Add a named capture for each of these keys where its value sits in the line, or move the key to `unresolved`.
